extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of Renaissance biography; literary scholars and historians evaluating biographical sources
extracted.subtask_description: Critical evaluation of biographical accounts of historical figures, focusing on source reliability, authorial bias, and textual evidence to judge intellectual attainment and factual accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carefully study autobiographical sources in context
rubrics_metrics.description: "It has seemed worth while to follow rather closely this account of his early years, as given chiefly by Erasmus himself... It must, however, be carefully studied in view of the circumstances under which it was written and by comparison with the little we can learn from other sources.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using an autobiographical source (e.g., the Grunnius letter), evaluate the circumstances of composition, the author's motives, and corroborate its claims against independent evidence. Treat such accounts as one piece of evidence, not definitive fact; perform cross-checks with other documentary or material records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat autobiographical narrative as literary artifice / rhetorical construction
rubrics_metrics.description: "his way of dressing up every subject he touched to suit the occasion."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect rhetorical shaping, exaggeration, and self-fashioning in personal accounts. Analyze tone, tropes, and dramatic devices; question passages that seem tailored to justify or embellish the author's position. Consider how the author’s literary aims affect factual reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer concrete facts over eloquent rhetoric when forming judgments
rubrics_metrics.description: "If one tries to form an opinion from facts rather than from words, one must feel that there is at least room for the question."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate between persuasive or elegiac language and verifiable facts. Base biographical conclusions primarily on documentary facts, known events, and material evidence rather than on the force or charm of the author's prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess intellectual attainment by close reading of texts (quotations, allusions, style)
rubrics_metrics.description: "This essay shows a very great acquisition, both of knowledge and of power... This essay shows a command of classic literature in quotation and allusion quite inconceivable except as a result of persistent study. Almost as much may be said of the style... it has already gained a very considerable degree of correctness and force.",
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge a subject's learning and development through internal textual markers: range and accuracy of quotations and allusions, command of sources, stylistic competence (correctness, force, vivacity), and evidence of sustained study. Use the work itself as primary evidence of intellectual formation.
